correctness.rationale: The all-positive labeling forces a family of disjoint loops and distinct undirected edges. Opposite orientations of an edge are logically identical and cannot be shattered together. A saturated support with at least one loop fails the labeling obtained by negating just that loop. Conversely any other permitted labeling is constructed by installing positive cycles, matching the even or odd set of negative-loop vertices internally (using an unqueried vertex in the odd case), and fixing leftovers. This proves all quantifiers and boundaries. Counting oriented pairs gives the exact face sum and exponential generating function; maximality and integral top homology follow from the explicit face structure. The sequential sampling formula has logarithm -2m(m-1)/n+o(1) at square-root scale. Direct independent exhaustive query tests for n=1,...,5 and facet counts agree.

originality.rationale: Unlike available fixed-point-free permutation / bipartite matching results, the self-inverse family identifies the two orientations of a transposition and admits fixed-point queries. The combination gives a distinct saturated-loop obstruction, a different exact exponential face series, complete facet spectrum, an integral top class and a square-root sampling exponent 2 rather than 1. The closest primary texts study involution patterns, matching counts or relative-order permutation shattering and do not imply these Boolean-trace statements. Searches were carried out against the current published record and accessible own claims; historical priority remains qualified, not certified.

value.rationale: The all-order classification describes exactly which individual entries of symmetric permutation matrices can be labeled independently, separating symmetric pairs and saturated fixed-point tests. It gives the complete bivariate exponential enumerator, a sharp full interval of facet sizes rather than merely a VC number, a unique nontrivial top integral homology class, and a natural factor-two change in the birthday-scale random sampling exponent. The object and parameters are canonical for involutions, and the classification has uses in capacity calculations and combinatorial topology; it is not a one-off unmotivated finite computation.
